verdict.reasoning: Patient states symptoms started about three days ago: "I think it was about three, it's been about three days now" and diarrhea is watery and frequent: "it's just coming out, like loads of it... super watery" and "I feel like it's like almost every hour, when I'm awake."

Pain is crampy, intermittent, central and lower: "I feel, I feel a cramp... around every hour I just feel something come up. And then I have to go" and location "it's like at the bottom" and "it feels pretty, like in the middle". Severity: patient suggests "maybe is that like a six, or a seven?"

Nausea/vomiting and milk association: "yeah I definitely feel kind of nauseous... I've have vomited" and "whenever I have like milk or something like that, I just feel like I want to vomit. And actually, yeah one time I just like had some milk, and I just completely vomited it."

Patient reports feeling hot without measuring temperature: "I think I am pretty, I feel kind of really hot all the time... I'm pretty sure I'm burning up... I haven't actually done any temperature reading."
Denies blood in stool: "Have you got any blood in your stools?" Patient: "no I don't, I don't remember anything... I think it's just... There's nothing like that."
Urination with decreased frequency: "are you passing urine OK?" Patient: "yeah a bit, I guess less frequently maybe. Um but yeah, it seems to be OK."

Drinking fluids but feels it goes straight through: "I'm trying to drink a lot of water" and later "it just feels like the, the fluids do go down. But it just feels like it's going straight through. It just feels like it's going straight through."
Ate lunch, stools still loose: "I had some lunch today. Um But again it just it just came, come out pretty loose."

Brother’s similar illness and course: "my brother has had, actually had something like this for um he has it as well for five days" and later "He's been like this for five days. I think he's getting better, but I'm not, I'm not really sure."

No past medical history: Doctor asks if otherwise fit and well; patient: "yeah I think, I think otherwise I'm fit and well" and "I can't think of any related medical history... no I I don't think so."
Paracetamol use as needed: "I haven't been, I'm not on any regular medication" followed by "I've been taking some like Paracetamols and stuff like that lately."
No known drug allergies: "And do you have any allergies to any medications?" Patient: "so I don't have any allergies that I know of."
Father with colon cancer and stage: "my dad actually has um colon cancer at the moment" and "he's sort of in his third stage." Stage 3 colon cancer is a direct interpretation of "third stage."
Living situation and work: "I live with my, um sister and my mum" and "I work at um an office, um in Central London. Um it's uh, so I work in government."
Social smoker: "I smoke, uh, uh for like socially, but not like regularly. Um... if it's a, a Friday or something like that I might, I might have a cigarette or something like that."

Occasional alcohol and binge 1–2 times/month: Describes modest weekday drinking and heavier sessions: "On Fridays I have more um alcohol" and "not every week, but maybe I'll once or twice a month, that yeah, I'll go out with my friends and drink a lot."
Trying to work despite symptoms: "Going to work with all of this. Um I dislike um, taking time off work. I feel like I I just want to go, um when I can. So I I try and go."

Doctor’s assessment matches: "your symptoms are suggestive of something called gastroenteritis" and history shows watery diarrhea for about 3 days, intermittent crampy abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, feeling hot, and denial of blood in stool as documented earlier.

Risk of dehydration: high stool frequency and reduced urine: diarrhea "almost every hour" and urination "less frequently maybe"; doctor notes concern: "you're losing a lot of fluid" and "if you are getting dehydrated then we need to do further investigations."
ORS/Dioralyte and clear fluids: "you can get things like Diarolyte, which is um, a fluid replacement you can get from the pharmacy" and earlier "Drink, make sure you drink plenty of fluids."
Soft diet advice: In response to food question, doctor says: "clear fluids. You can use soft diet, things like soup, mash. And then gradually build up, um as much as your body can tolerate."

Paracetamol for fever/pain: "You can try just you know regular Paracetamol if you are feeling feverish" and later: "If you are having, if you've got a bit of tummy pain, if you're feeling feverish, then I think Paracetamol is very sensible."
Alcohol advice: "Try and avoid alcohol if you can."

Safety net 48 hours and further evaluation: "if your symptoms aren't settling down in the next couple of days, so forty eight hours, I want you to give me a call back" and "if you are getting dehydrated then we need to do further investigations."

Emphasis on fluids/ORS for dehydration risk: Doctor repeatedly stresses fluids and ORS: "Drink, make sure you drink plenty of fluids"; recommends "Diarolyte, which is a fluid replacement" and links dehydration to need for further investigations.

Follow-up timeframe: "if your symptoms aren't settling down in the next couple of days, so forty eight hours, I want you to give me a call back" and "I think let's, let's see how you are in the next one to two days."
